history.content: MMU stands for Manned Maneuvering Unit. It's a nitrogen propelled backpack that allows astronauts to fly with precision.

Here are some quick facts about astronauts:
1. The term “astronaut” derives from the Greek words meaning “star sailor".
2. Since inception, NASA has selected 360 astronaut candidates, including 299 men and 61 women.
3. There have been continuous human presences at the International Space Station since Expedition 1 arrived on Nov. 2, 2000, with usually seven astronauts living on board at any given time
4. The first class of NASA astronauts, known as the Mercury 7, was selected in 1959.
5. More than 12,000 people applied to be an astronaut between March 2 and March 31, 2020.

To become an astronaut, you must meet the following qualifications:
1. Be a U.S. citizen
2. Have a master's degree in a STEM field, including engineering, biological science, physical science, computer science or mathematics, from an accredited institution.
3. Have a minimum of three years of related professional experience obtained after degree completion (or 1,000 Pilot-in-Command hours with at least 850 of those hours in high performance jet aircraft for pilots)
4. Be able to successfully complete the NASA long-duration flight astronaut physical.
Note that NASA accepts applications for the Astronaut Candidate Program on an as-needed basis, and in recent years, new astronaut candidates have been selected approximately every four years.
